messages:
alex: Heads up — console charts are freezing when I apply a time-range filter on the canary. Started ~10:12 UTC after the deploy. Anyone seeing this?

maria: Yup, saw it on canary too. Heatmap + timeseries with live-stream toggled on. UI CPU spike and jank for 3–10s.

dave: Telemetry alerts show repeated_fetches sampler spike. Telemetry client logs a bunch of identical network retries and GC pauses.

alex: I can repro locally with the canary bundle. Flame graph shows charting lib re-initializing a few times instead of reusing instances — smells like chunking/caching issue.

ryan: Which PR touched chunking? I pushed a change yesterday that reordered prefetch priority and changed chunk naming (#4322). Could be related.

maria: From the browser console: TypeError during rehydrate: "Cannot read property 'length' of undefined" when sparkline buffer is processed. Also seeing: "Chunk load duplicated: chart-v2.js x3" repeated.

alex: Sample logs from repro:```
[ui] fetch /api/v1/chart-data?t=161772
[ui] chunk chart-v2.js loaded
[ui] chunk chart-v2.js loaded
[ui] init ChartLib v2.7.4
[ui] GC: major pause 120ms
```

dave: @opsbot can we rollback the canary deploy while we triage?

opsbot: deploy-bot: rollback initiated for service=console-canary -> target=previous-successful. started_at=1748015800. ETA ~90s.

jenna: My hunch: prefetch changed ordering + chunk filename/contenthash caused the prefetcher to request the same module under different names concurrently, which defeats the KV cache dedupe and causes duplicate parser/initialization. Also prefetch concurrency being high floods the main thread.

ryan: Confirmed I switched to contenthash to avoid stale bundles. Didn't realize prefetch dedupe relied on filenames. I can revert chunk naming strategy or we can change prefetch dedupe to use module ids.

alex: Proposed short-term fix: (1) rollback prefetch concurrency to 3, (2) dedupe by module id in prefetch layer, (3) add a small guard in chart init to no-op if already initialized. I'll open a PR for the fixes.

dave: After rollback, canary metrics improved immediately — 99p latency for chart interactions dropped from ~3.2s to ~120ms. CPU/JSHeap stable.

opsbot: deploy-bot: rollback complete at=1748015875. monitoring status=green.

jenna: :thumbsup: We should add an integration test: simulate loading dashboard with heatmap + live-stream and assert no duplicate chunk requests and no reinit cycles. Also add a telemetry alert that correlates repeated_fetches with GC spikes.

alex: Agreed. I'll add the CI test and the PR is #4331. Assigning reviewers: @ryan @jenna. Will also add a short blurb to the release notes and an ops-runbook step for future chunk-name transitions.

jenna: Thanks — nice catch.

ryan: Thanks team, fixing now.
